πτύον.long: a simple wooden pitchfork; a winnowing-shovel or fan.
πτύον.as:
** πτύον, -ου, τό,
[in Sm.: Is 30:24*;]
a winnowing shovel or fan: Mt 3:12, Lk 3:17.†

πτερύγιον.der: neuter of a presumed derivative of G4420 (πτέρυξ);
πτερύγιον.as:
πτερύγιον, -ου, -τό
(dimin. of πτέρυξ), [in LXX chiefly for כָּנָף;]
1.a little wing.
2. Anything like a wing, as a turret, battlement: τ. ἱεροῦ, Mt 4:5, Lk 4:9.†

πτωχός.long: poor, destitute, spiritually poor, either in a good sense (humble devout persons) or bad.
πτωχός.sd: akin to G4422 (πτοέω) and the alternate of G4098 (πίπτω)); a beggar (as cringing), i.e. pauper (strictly denoting absolute or public mendicancy, although also used in a qualified or relative sense; whereas G3993 (πένης) properly means only straitened circumstances in private), literally (often as noun) or figuratively (distressed)
πτωχός.as:
πτωχός, -ή, -όν
(< πτώσσω, to crouch, cower), [in LXX for עָנִי, דַּל, רָשׁ, etc.;]
of one who crouches and cowers, hence,
1. as subst., a beggar: Lk 14:13, 2116:20, 22.
2. As adj.,
(a) prop., beggarly: metaph., στοιχεῖα, Ga 4:9 (v. Lft., in l.);
(b) in broader sense (opp. to πλούσιος), poor: Mt 11:519:2126:9, 11, Mk 10:2112:42, 4314:5, 7, Lk 4:187:2218:2219:821:3, Jo 12:5, 6, 813:29, Ro 15:26, II Co 6:10, Ga 2:10, Ja 2:2, 3, 6, Re 13:16; π. τ. κόσμῳ, Ja 2:5; metaph., Lk 6:20, Re 3:17; π. τ. πνεύματι, Mt 5:3.†
SYN.: πένης, q.v.

πτῶσις.sd: a crash, i.e. downfall (literally or figuratively)
πτῶσις.as:
πτῶσις, -εως, ἡ
(< πίπτω), [in LXX chiefly for נֶגֶף, מַפֶּלֶת, and cogn. forms;]
a falling, fall (Plat., Plut., al.): Mt 7:27; metaph., Lk 2:34.†

πτῶμα.long: a fall; a carcass, corpse, dead body.
πτῶμα.sd: a ruin, i.e. (specially), lifeless body (corpse, carrion)
πτῶμα.as:
πτῶμα, -τος, τό
(< πίπτω), [in LXX: Jg 14:8 (מַפֶּלֶת), Jb 16:15 (14) (פֶּרֶץ), Is 51:19 (שֹׁד), Jth 8:19, Wi 4:18, al.;]
1.a fall, metaph., a misfortune, calamity (Trag., Plat., Polyb., al.; LXX).
2. That which has fallen;
(a) of buildings, a ruin (Polyb.);
(b) of living creatures, in cl. (poët. only) usually c. gen., νεκρῶν, etc., but also absol., as in late writers and NT, a fallen body, a carcase, corpse: Mt 14:1224:28, Mk 15:45; π. αὐτοῦ, Mk 6:29; αὐτῶν, Re 11:8, 9 (cf. Rutherford, NPhr., 472 f.).†

πτέρυξ.der: from a derivative of G4072 (πέτομαι) (meaning a feather);
πτέρυξ.as:
πτέρυξ, -υγος, ἡ
(< πέτομαι), [in LXX chiefly for כָּנָף;]
a wing: of birds, Mt 23:37, Lk 13:34, Re 12:14; of creatures seen in a vision, Re 4:89:9.†

πτύω.as:
πτύω,
[in LXX: Nu 12:14 (ירק), Si 28:12*;]
to spit: Mk 7:338:23, Jo 9:6 (cf. ἐκ-, ἐμ-πτύω).†

πτύσσω.long: I fold, roll up (as a scroll).
πτύσσω.sd: and thus apparently allied to G4072 (πέτομαι) through the idea of expansion, and to 4429 through that of flattening; compare G3961 (πατέω)); to fold, i.e. furl a scroll
πτύσσω.as:
* πτύσσω,
to fold; of a scroll, to roll up: βιβλίον, Lk 4:20 (cf. ἀνα-πτύσσω).†

πτοέομαι.long: I terrify, scare, strike with panic.
πτοέομαι.der: probably akin to the alternate of G4098 (πίπτω) (through the idea of causing to fall) or to G4072 (πέτομαι) (through that of causing to fly away);
πτοέομαι.as:
πτοέω, -ῶ,
[in LXX chiefly for חתת ni.;]
to terrify. Pass., to be terrified: Lk 21:924:37 (WH, mg., θροηθέντες).†

πτύσμα.as:
* πτύσμα, -τος, τό,
(< πτύω),
spittle: Jo 9:6 (Hipp., Polyb., al.).†

πτέρνα.as:
πτέρνα, -ης, ἡ,
[in LXX for עָקֵב;]
the heel: fig., ἐπαίρειν τὴν π. ἐπί, Jo 13:18(LXX).†

Πτολεμαΐς.long: Ptolemais, a coast city of Phoenicia, midway between Tyre and Caesarea.
Πτολεμαΐς.der: from (Ptolemy, after whom it was named);
Πτολεμαΐς.as:
Πτολεμαΐς, -ΐδος, ἡ,
Ptolemais, a maritime city of Phœnicea: Ac 21:7.†

πταίω.long: I stumble, fall, sin, err, transgress.
πταίω.sd: to trip, i.e. (figuratively) to err, sin, fail (of salvation)
πταίω.as:
πταίω,
[in LXX chiefly for נגף ni.;]
1. trans., to cause to stumble (I Ki 4:3, cf. Deiss., BS, 681).
2. Intrans., to stumble. Metaph., in moral sense, Ro 11:11, Ja 2:103:2, II Pe 1:10.†

πτηνόν.as:
** πτηνός, -ή, -όν
(< πέτομαι), [in Aq.: Jb 5:7*;]
winged; as subst., τὰ π., birds: I Co 15:39.†

πτωχεία.as:
πτωχεία, -ας, ἡ
(< πτωχεύω), [in LXX chiefly for עֳנִי;]
beggary, destitution: II Co 8:2, 9, Re 2:9.†

πτωχεύω.long: I am in poverty, am a beggar.
πτωχεύω.sd: to be a beggar, i.e. (by implication) to become indigent (figuratively)
πτωχεύω.as:
πτωχεύω
(< πτωχός), [in LXX: Jg 6:6, Ps 78 (79):8 (דּלל); Jg 14:15 A, Pr 23:21 (ירשׁ); Ps 33 (34):10 (רוּשׁ), To 4:21*;]
1.to be a beggar, to beg (so chiefly in cl.).
2.to be poor as a beggar, to be destitute, poor: opp. to πλούσιος ὤν, II Co 8:9.†

πτύρομαι.der: from a presumed derivative of G4429 (πτύω) (and thus akin to G4422 (πτοέω));
πτύρομαι.as:
* πτύρομαι, depon.,
to be startled, frightened: Phl 1:28. (The active πτύρω is also found in some late writers.)†

πτόησις.as:
πτόησις, -εως, ἡ
(< πτοέω), [in LXX: Pr 3:25 (פַּחַד), Sir 50:4 א1, I Mac 3:25 R*;]
a fluttering, excitement, caused by any emotion, but esp. by fear, hence, terror: φοβεῖσθαι πτόησιν, to be afraid with (cogn. acc.) or of any terror (v. ICC, in l.): I Pe 3:6.†
